header:
Date: 2027-04-08
Time: 10:00 - 11:00 PDT
Duration: ~60 minutes
Location: Zoom
Meeting type: SE/AE enablement session (internal)
Agenda: 1) Messaging refresh 2) Competitive positioning 3) Live demo practice + feedback
Attendees: Maya (AE), Evan (SE), Priya (SE), Liam (Product), ~12 observers (internal)
summary: Internal SE/AE enablement focused on refining messaging for Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private, sharpening competitive differentiation vs major cloud offerings, and running live demo practice with timed use-cases. Key outcomes: action items assigned to update collateral, schedule recorded practice demos, and produce objection handling sheet.
topics: Messaging: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
Objection handling: security, data residency, cost
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: okay everyone thanks for joining, let's kick off, agenda is messaging, competitive, then demo practice, we wanna keep tight timings, right?
[00:12] Evan: yep, I'll lead the competitive slides and then do a quick demo with the shared sandbox, forgive the glitch if the recording lags, my wifi is meh.
[00:25] Priya: quick ask, can we call out more clearly the difference between Dedicated and Private in one sentence? customers keep confusing them.
[00:33] Liam: yeah one-liner suggestion: Dedicated = reserved GPU capacity with an SLA; Private = customer-managed control plane + VPC/on-prem. short.
[00:45] Maya: love it, keep it pithy. also call out cost tradeoffs, like Dedicated gives predictable throughput -> easier to budget, Hosted is best for quick go-to-market.
[01:02] Evan: when we talk competitive, customers ask about OpenAI and Anthropic first. they ask: \"why not just use OpenAI?\" we need to hit three points: predictable latency/SLA, cost controls (batching/quantization), and private deployment options for regulated data.
[01:20] Priya: also audit logs, SSO/SAML, and KMS integration - enterprise checklist. put SOC 2 and ISO on the slide. sometimes transcribed as SOX but it's SOC 2.
[01:34] Maya: call that out under security. quick poll — who uses price vs latency as the lead pitch?
[01:40] (short chatter)
[02:00] Evan: i think for infra/platform buyers we lead with economics: per-token cost and predictable throughput; for product teams we lead with latency and reliability.
[02:15] Maya: good distinction. ok demo practice: we're doing two scenarios, the first is low-latency chat assistant for customer support (target p50 <150ms token), second is embeddings + reranking for semantic search at scale. Evan you're demoing scenario one.
[02:36] Evan: cool, starting the demo — heads-up, I'm using the hosted api but I'll mention how the same API maps to Dedicated and Private.
[02:45] [demo audio - keyboard clacking, screen share starts]
[03:05] Evan: here we send a streaming call, you can see the tokens come back incrementally — this is great for chat apps where perceived latency matters. note we also do prefix caching so repeated queries are faster.
[03:25] Priya: can we show the console latency breakdown? customers love that graph.
[03:30] Evan: yep opening the console, ok there's token-level cost, CPU vs GPU time, and per-route p50/p95. sometimes the console name gets transcribed as Redwood Console or Redwood Consol.
[03:50] Maya: small nit — when you show cost, please call out quantization and batching recommendations for savings; folks always ask, \"how much can we save?\" have ballpark numbers.
[04:05] Evan: i'll say typical savings range 20-50% depending on model and workload, with quantization plus batching and cache.
[04:20] Liam: make sure to caveat: savings depend on accuracy budget; we shouldn't promise numbers, say 'up to'.
[04:35] Evan: switching to competitive slide — here we map features: SLA, private deploy, per-token price, tooling. competitors: OpenAI (great model quality), Anthropic (safety/guardrails), Cohere (embeddings focus), major clouds like AWS Bedrock / Vertex AI (tighter infra integrations).
[04:55] Priya: customers ask about bringing their own models, how do we position that vs self-hosting?
[05:05] Evan: pitch: Redwood gives the unified runtime + ops layer so you get production-grade serving without building the infra. self-hosting requires hiring infra + ops, and you miss our batching/caching/quality monitoring features.
[05:20] Maya: call out the migration path: start with Hosted to validate, move to Dedicated for predictable SLAs, then Private for strict compliance. that's a clear progression.
[05:34] [audience question briefly muffled]
[05:50] Priya: practice objection: \"Your cost is higher than OpenAI.\" how do we handle?
[05:58] Maya: answer: show unit economics — we provide controls to lower per-token costs (batching, quantization, KV cache), plus predictable throughput and SLAs. risk-adjusted cost is lower when reliability matters.
[06:20] Evan: add that we avoid vendor lock via model catalog flexibility and give model version pinning and rollouts.
[06:32] Priya: another objection: \"We need on-prem due to regs.\" we say: Private deployments + KMS/HSM + audit logs, we support air-gapped packages.
[06:47] Evan: practice demo — i'm going to simulate a latency spike and show fallback routing to a cheaper model variant; note this gets noisy in the transcript because the recording lags.
[07:05] [demo - simulated spike, screen shows routing config]
[07:30] Evan: okay fallback engaged, traffic moved to a compatible model variant — we keep responses within acceptable quality.
[07:45] Maya: good call to show A/B and canary rollouts in the console. customers love seeing the rollback button.
[08:00] Priya: feedback on Evan's delivery: you speed through the slides, slow down on the savings examples and the security bullet points. also avoid jargon like KV cache without a one-liner explanation.
[08:20] Evan: noted. i'll add a brief line: \"KV cache stores previously computed key/value states so follow-up tokens are faster\".
[08:35] Maya: let's role-play a tough buyer — Liam you'll be a platform lead asking about data residency and audit trails.
[08:45] Liam: okay — \"We need region-restricted data with SOC 2 and quarterly audits, can you comply?\"
[08:54] Evan: yes, we offer regional deployments, SOC 2 attestation, and configurable audit log retention. for Private, customers can manage KMS/HSM.
[09:05] Liam: follow-up: \"How about e-discovery and long-term retention?\"
[09:10] Priya: we recommend a separate logging pipeline to your SIEM and configurable retention policies.
[09:18] [short laughter]
[09:25] Maya: ok second scenario now, embeddings + reranking. Evan, set the stage: large corpus, daily indexing, latency for rerank ~200ms per query.
[09:35] Evan: showing ingestion pipeline... we recommend hybrid storage: store vectors in customer's vector DB + use Redwood for embeddings generation with batching. use caching for hot queries.
[09:50] Priya: customers ask: why not run embeddings on dedicated infra they already own?
[09:58] Evan: you can, but we manage scaling for peak indexing and provide cost-optimization hints; plus we integrate with popular vector DBs.
[10:15] Maya: demo hiccup — the search ranking UI didn't render in time; keep going, call that out as \"demo environment fluke\".
[10:30] Evan: noted. moving on to critique: timing, maybe break demos into 8 minute chunks with 3 minute Q&A each.
[10:40] Priya: agree, and have a sticky slide with top 5 objection responses.
[10:45] Evan: i'll draft that.
[10:52] Maya: ok we ran out of time for full feedback, but quick round-robin: what	 s one thing each of you will change next time?
[11:00] Evan: slow down on cost examples, add savings ranges as \"up to\" and include a small note on tradeoffs.
[11:06] Priya: add a 1-line explainer for technical terms on every slide.
[11:12] Liam: include a one-slide flow for migration path: Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private.
[11:18] Maya: perfect — action items recapped in chat, i'll follow up with calendar invites for recorded practice sessions. thanks everyone.
[11:30] [meeting ends, some cross chatter and screen close sounds]
notes: This transcript is an internal enablement session; transcription includes some mis-hearings and typical filler words. Demo environment flukes noted and will be resolved before customer-facing rehearsals.
